title: Redwood Monthly All-Hands - October 2026
summary: Leadership update and company metrics. Product roadmap highlights (Redwood Optimize, Dedicated autoscale improvements), Dedicated & Private customer updates, hiring and headcount plan, quarterly revenue and usage trends, upcoming compliance work (SOC 2 re-audit), and a long Q&A about pricing, on-call rotations, and rollout cadence. Session ends with action items: publish roadmap doc, schedule SOC 2 deep-dive, update on-call schedule.
topics: Redwood Optimize rollout and savings case studies
Private deployment progress and SOC 2 re-audit
Hiring, org updates, and on-call rotations
Customer success stories and case studies
transcript:
[00:00] Leah Kim: Good morning everyone, thanks for joining, uh this is our October all hands, we'll run about 70, 75 minutes, um Jordan's gonna kick off with the business update then we'll go into product and ops.
[00:30] Jordan Lee: Hey team, thanks. Quick headline, Q3 closed slightly ahead of plan, usage growth is up 22% quarter over quarter, we saw a big spike in embeddings usage from a new mid-market cohort, um revenue is trending in line with plan, burn is stable. Shoutout to sales and platform for the BizDev motions.
[01:10] Miguel Santos: Just to add, infra ran hot on a few days during the index rebuilds, we patched an autoscaler bug which helped, latency p95 improved about 12% in the last two weeks after the kernel selection change.
[01:40] Leah Kim: Nice. Product — quick roadmap bullets: Redwood Optimize is out of private beta, we're doing staged rollout to hosted customers this month, the batching suggestions UI will go live next week. Also Dedicated autoscale now supports burst capacity policies in preview.
[02:05] Priya Das: Quick note, customers on Dedicated are asking about predictable tail latency; we did a perf run versus two competitors and our median is comparable but our 99th is better except when KV cache misses stack up — still work to do.
[02:35] Samir Patel: On the research side we landed a quantization path that saves ~2-2.5x on token cost for some T5-style models, but it's tricky on very long sequences, so guidance will be model-dependent.
[03:10] Employee (Audience): Quick question — SOC 2 status?
[03:16] Avery Brooks: SOC 2 re-audit is scheduled for mid-November, docs are almost ready, control owners we need to confirm evidence for change management and incident response. We'll follow up with a calendar invite for a control walkthrough.
[03:45] Jordan Lee: On sales operations, pipeline looks healthy; we closed two Dedicated deals for finance customers with strict VPC requirements — thanks to SEs for the privacy review loops.
[04:10] Leah Kim: Now product demo — quick tour of Optimize savings dashboard, um note the example case where a customer saved 38% by switching quantization + smarter batching. The UI will show cost delta, quality impact and recommended rollout steps.
[05:00] Priya Das: There was some confusion about 'recommended rollout steps' in the beta docs — we'll update wording to include canary sizes and evaluation prompts.
[05:30] Miguel Santos: Autoscaler detail — we added a capacity reservation layer so Dedicated customers can keep baseline throughput even during cluster rebalances, that should address some of the tail latency complaints.
[06:05] Employee: Is Private on-prem support still on track for the regulatory pilot?
[06:12] Samir Patel: Yes, the on-prem package for the pilot team is ready, the integration with customer KMS/HSM needs one more test; we've done two internal end-to-end runs.
[06:40] Jordan Lee: A note about pricing — we're experimenting with a new dedicated pricing SKU for sustained reserved pools with committed bursts; this is still internal, don't circulate yet.
[07:05] Leah Kim: Hiring — we closed IC hiring for infra and two PM hires starting in November, we still need senior SE and support engineers, hiring is the highest priority for product and infra.
[07:30] Priya Das: Customer stories — one of our customers (pseudonym: HelixCorp) used Optimize to cut inference costs and accelerated their pilot to production in two weeks; CSM will publish a light case study.
[08:00] Q&A segment opens — we had about 30 live questions, selected common ones below.
[08:15] Employee: On-call cadence — will it change with the new autoscaler?
[08:20] Miguel Santos: We're proposing a 4-person on-call rotation per region, with infra and platform triage shifts; more details in the doc we'll share, aim to reduce paging for non-sev1.
[08:55] Employee: Are we prioritizing private deployments over hosted features?
[09:00] Jordan Lee: Not deprioritizing — we see both as growth vectors: hosted drives usage and low-friction PLG adoption, Private/Dedicated brings bigger contracts and enterprise credibility. Roadmap balances both.
[09:40] Leah Kim: Product question — what metrics will we surface for Optimize adoption?
[09:45] Priya Das: We'll track percentage of requests using recommended batch/quant profiles, cost savings per month, and quality regressions via evals on prompt sets.
[10:20] Employee: Any competitor moves to call out?
[10:25] Jordan Lee: A few companies are marketing similar batching/optimizer tooling; main competitor mentions: MajorCloudAI, OpenServe, and QuantifyAI — our edge is the runtime/observability combo and the unified rollout tools.
[11:00] Leah Kim: Ops update — dashboard retention tiers are being refactored to save storage costs, users on free tier will see 7 day window, paid tiers keep longer retention.
[11:30] Employee: Security question — SSO and SCIM support timeline?
[11:35] Avery Brooks: SSO (SAML/OIDC) and SCIM are GA for enterprise accounts as of last quarter; we're working on improved RBAC and attribute mapping for the next patch.
[12:05] Leah Kim: Wrap-up points: publish Q4 roadmap doc, schedule SOC 2 evidence walkthrough, finalize on-call rotation doc, and post hiring update.
[12:30] Jordan Lee: Thanks all, appreciate the hard work. We'll post the recording and slides.
[12:45] Meeting ends. Note: transcription contains some partial words and mistakes — e.g., 'KV cache' read as 'K V cache' in places, and some speaker labels merged.
